tex_content.html:
Lemma
[Surface coarea identity] 1. ch16:16.77–16.78\group chapter-16 For $g\in C^1(\mathcal G_ ho )$ and almost every $ ho \in (0,R)$,

egin{equation} \int _{\partial \mathcal G_ ho } g\, ds = D_ ho \int _{\mathcal G_ ho } g|\delta r|\, dA ag {16.77} \end{equation}

where \[ r(X) = |X - Y|, \qquad X \in \mathbb R^3. \] For such regular radii,

egin{equation} ag {16.78} \partial \widetilde{\mathscr {S}}_{ ho } = \widetilde{\mathscr {S}}_{ ho } \cap \{ X \in \mathbb {R}^{3}\mid |X-Y|= ho \} = igcup _{j=1}^{n( ho )} \Gamma _{ ho }^{(j)} \end{equation}

where the $\Gamma _ ho ^{(j)}$ are simple closed $C^2$ curves.
Proof

\sketch Sard’s theorem gives $\delta r e 0$ on the boundary for almost every $ ho $. On the annulus $\widetilde{\mathscr G}=\widetilde{\mathscr S}_ ho \setminus \widetilde{\mathscr S}_{ ho -\varepsilon }$, orient the tangent by $\mathbf t= u imes \delta r/|\delta r|$ on the outer boundary and with the opposite sign on the inner boundary. Extend $ u imes \delta r/|\delta r|$ to a $C^1$ field $\mathbf F$ and apply (16.68) with the cutoff field $\varepsilon ^{-1}(r- ho +\varepsilon )g\mathbf F$. The boundary term is the difference quotient of $\int _{\mathcal G_ ho }g|\delta r|\, dA$; all remaining annular terms tend to zero. Letting $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ gives (16.77).

□
The main Hölder estimate will be a consequence of estimates for the integral \[ \D ( ho ; Z), \] which is defined for $Z \in \Gscr $ and $ ho > 0$ by \[ \D ( ho ; Z)=\int _{\Sscr _{ ho }(Z)} |\delta \varphi |^2\, dA. \]

(cf. the Dirichlet integral used in Chapter 12). $\Lambda _1$ denotes a constant such that

egin{equation} ag {16.79} \A (\Sscr _{3R/4}(Y)) \le \Lambda _1 (3R/4)^2. \end{equation}
